title: I linked Gemini Notebook to Gemini and queried 4 research notebooks in one chat thread
excerpt: I could finally reference multiple notebooks with this trick
content_html:
Published Oct 24, 2026, 3:00 PM EDT

I cover Android with a focus on productivity, automation, and Google’s ecosystem, including Gemini and everyday apps. With a background in engineering and software development, I tend to go beyond surface-level tips.
Before joining AP, I wrote for tech publications such as Gizbot in 2023 and iJunkie (formerly known as iPhoneHacks) from 2021 to 2022.

Gemini Notebook works strictly with the sources you give it, whether they are PDFs, Google Docs files, or notes, and helps you reason within that material.

That constraint is what makes Gemini Notebook feel trustworthy. However, it also exposes its biggest limitation. Each notebook exists in isolation, with no way to cross-reference the other.

If I had financial documents in one notebook and long-term goals in another, I couldn't ask questions about both.

That's where Gemini comes in. With Gemini's ability to reference multiple Gemini Notebook notebooks in a single chat, that wall finally came down.

After I started using them together, Gemini Notebook felt far more powerful than before.

Gemini Notebook's biggest strength is also its biggest weakness

The limitation that kept showing up

Gemini Notebook only works with the sources you give it. It doesn't pull in outside information or try to fill gaps with guesses. That makes its answers feel grounded.

When it points out a pattern or summarizes an idea, you can trace it to a document you uploaded.

However, each notebook is isolated from the others. To connect ideas effectively, you must manually combine documents into a single notebook.

Notes I write today often relate to documents I uploaded months ago in a different notebook. So when I tried to connect those dots, everything broke down.

Pairing Gemini Notebook with Gemini

How Gemini changes the equation

With Gemini's ability to add multiple Gemini Notebook notebooks to a single conversation, I no longer have to merge everything into one massive notebook.

Using it is straightforward. First, open the Gemini website in a browser. Click the + icon in the message box and select Gemini Notebook. From there, you can choose multiple notebooks and select Add.

After attaching the notebooks, you can ask Gemini questions about all of them at once, like you would in a normal conversation.

Now, Gemini acts as a connective layer, letting insights flow between notebooks that were never designed to communicate.

That means I can keep my notebooks laser-focused, while Gemini handles the cross-referencing.

You can also attach and reference notebooks in the Gemini mobile app. In the Gemini mobile app, tap the attachment (+) icon.

How I use this pairing in everyday situations

Where the Gemini Notebook and Gemini combination shines

The real benefit of using Gemini Notebook with Gemini shows up in daily scenarios, especially when your data is spread across different notebooks and formats.

If I'm working on a long-term project, such as a move, budget planning, or a big work assignment, my information is rarely available in one place.

I know that multiple notebooks have information I want to reference, so I add them to a single Gemini chat. I might add notebooks with my personal finance goals, journal entries, and a third with relevant work emails and message threads.

With Gemini pulling them into a single conversation, I can ask questions that span all three.

For instance, whether my goals are realistic given current expenses, or how a work deadline clashes with something I've flagged as important in my journal.

Gemini pulls context from all the notebooks at once, and I get answers that reflect the full picture.

Turning notebooks into a better learning system

My notes finally feel connected

Before pairing Gemini Notebook with Gemini, most of my old notebooks were effectively archives.

I organized sources and extracted summaries, but when a project ended, I rarely used those notes again.

Cross-referencing notebooks through Gemini changes that dynamic.

When I add multiple notebooks to a Gemini chat, older material becomes relevant again because it connects to what I'm working on now.

A question about a current problem might surface insights from a notebook I hadn't opened in months.

The best part is that I don't need to reorganize or rewrite anything. Gemini does the connective work, pulling context from across notebooks only when it's needed.

As a result, I'm more comfortable keeping notebooks focused, knowing they won't become dead ends.

Even rough or incomplete sources feel worth saving, because they can contribute later when viewed alongside other notebooks.

A bonus is that I can export the conversation to Google Docs. All it takes is clicking the three-dot menu icon below the chat and selecting Export to Docs.

Exporting conversations instantly turns cross-notebook insights into an editable, shareable document.

The unlikely pairing that upgraded my Gemini Notebook experience

Gemini Notebook is still where I make sense of lengthy PDFs, articles, emails, and documents.

Using it with Gemini supercharges the experience by letting me reference multiple notebooks at a time.

The most significant difference is that I no longer feel pressured to over-organize or predict future use cases.

I can keep notebooks focused and even a little messy, knowing they won't become dead ends.

When I need to make sense of something, whether it's learning across subjects, scattered notes, or revisiting old ideas, Gemini lets me analyze more than one notebook.
